III., Oct., 1923; regiar., sup. ct., Penang, Dec., 1924; asst. offr. assigne, Penang, in addn., Apr. to July and Oct. to Nov., 1925; cls. I.B., Apr., 1928; solr.-genl., S.S., Apr., 1928; temp. puinane judge, Sept. to Nov., 1930 and Jan to Fea., 1931; ag. atty.-gen., Apr., 1932.

MILLS, LAURENCE LANGLEY.—B. 1890; ed. Dover coll.; pol. prob., F.M.S., 1910; asst. comsnr., police, F.M.S., 1914; ag. o/c Malay States Guide depot and asst. comsnr., police North Perak, 1917-18; ch. pol. offr., Pahang, 1920-1923; ag. comsnr., police, Johore, 1924-1925; ag. comsnr. police, Trengganu, 1927-29; dep. const. police, F.M.S., 1928; dep. comsnr., pol. ch. pol. offr., Pahang, Sept., 1930.

MILNE, GEOFFREY, M.Sc. (Leeds), F.I.C.—B. 1898; ed. Hymers Coll., Hull and Leeds Univ.; mily. serv., 1917-19; asst., later lecture, Leeds Univ., Sept., 1923; soil chemist, E. Ainsworth, agrl. research sta., Amani, Tanganyika Territory, Sept., 1928.

MILNE, T. M.—B. 1890; dep. regiar. gen. and dep. regiar. and dep. marshal, sup. ct. and regiar., friendly societies, Trinidad, Sept., 1931; asst. crown solr., 1932.

MILSTEAD, HERBERT ERNEST GEORGE.—B. 1886; temp. asst. acct., P.W.D., Uganda, May-July, 1921; asst. treas., Kenya, July, 1921; visiting just., Nairobi prison, 1922; sec. tender bd., 1923 and 1927; ag. senr. asst. treas., in 1924 and 1927; seconded to secretariat as ass. offr., June, 1925 to Apr., 1926; ag. acct., treas., May to July, 1927; asst. currency offr., July, 1927; ch. storekeeper, P.W.D., Nov., 1929.

MILTON, SIR W. H., K.C.M.G. (1906), K.C.V.O. (1910), C.M.G. (1901).—B. 1844; clk., col. sec.'s office, Cape, Apr., 1858; 3rd class clk., 1st Jan., 1879; 2nd class clk., Jan., 1881; 1st class clk., Apr., 1883; sec. to the tender bd., 1881; clk. to exec. coun., 1883; ch. clk. and acctnt., col. sec.'s office, 1883; sec. to prime min., Mar., 1894; detached for serv. in Rhodesia as ch. sec. and sec. serv., Oct., 1897; ag. admir. Rhod. July, 1897 to Nov., 1898; apptd. admistr. Mashonaland and senr. admistr. S. Rhodesia, Dec., 1898; admistr. S. Rhodesia, 20th Dec., 1902; resig., 1914.

MINTER, K. S. —B. 1894; apptd. after compt. exam. asst. clk., and assigned to G.P.O., Sept., 1912; apptd. after compt. exam. clk. of the 2nd div. of the civ. serv., and assigned to H.M. stationery office, Aug., 1914; to C.O., Oct., 1914; cler. offr., higher grade, 1st Apr., 1922.

MITCHELL, EDWARD THOMAS.—B. 1904; mily. ser., May, 1918 to Jan., 1919; temp. c.t. W.O., Feb., 1919 to Aug., 1926; apptd. to C.O. as cler. offr. after compt. exam. (Southborough), Aug., 1926.

MITCHELL, HON. SIR JAMES, K.C.M.G. (1921), C.M.G. (1917); M.L.A., W. Australia—B. 1866; entd. ser. of W. Aust. Bank; 16th man. of Northam branch; entd. parlmt., 1906; hon. min. and mem. of exec. coun., 1906; min. agric., 1907; min. for lands in addition to act. 1909, and again in 1916; premier, 1919-24 as since Apr., 1930.

MITCHELL, PHILIP EUGEN, C.M.G. (1921), M.C.—Ed. St. Paul's Schl. and Trinity Coll.; asst. res., Nyasaland, 1912; lect., K.A.R., 1915; capt., 1917; adjt., 1917-18; mem. in desps.; A.D.C. and pvt. sec. to ag. gov., Nyasaland, 1918-19; asst. polit. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 1919; asst. sec., native affrs., prov. comsnr., 1928; sec. for native affrs., 1928.
MITCHELSON, Hon. Sir Edwin, K.C.M.G. (1921).—B. 1846; ed. St. Matthew's Ch. of Eng. Schl. and privately; M.H.R., N.Z., 1881-1896; min. of pub. wks., 1883-4 and 1887-9; min. of native affrs., 1887-91; postmr.-gen. and comnr. of telegraphs, 1889-91; M.L.C., 1920; has been mem., chmn., etc., of many local bodies and organizations in N.Z.; Knight of Grace of Order of St. John of Jerusalem, 1910.

MOIR, John Innes.—B. 1897; ed. Gordon's Coll. and Univ., Aberdeen; M.B., Ch.B., 1921; D.P.H., 1923; surg.-sub. lieut., R.N.V.R., European War; lieut., R.A.M.C., 1921; house surg., Sick Children's Hosp., Aberdeen, 1921; asst. M.O. City Hosp., Aberdeen, 1921-23; M.O. for Falkland Is. Coy., 1923-27; P.M.O., Falkland Is. govt., Feb., 1929; capt., Falkland Is. Def. Force, 1929; major and O.C. from May, 1930.

MOIR, STEDMAN ESDALE.—Clk., P.O., St. Kitts, Mar., 1904; rev. offr., Nevis, Apr., 1906; clk. to mag., Dist. "C," St. Kitts, 1913; served with H.M. Forces, 1916-19; on active service, 28th London Regt., 1916-17; cotton inspr., St. Kitts, ag. audit olk., May to Sept., 1922; cashier, treas. dept., St. Kitts, Oct., 1922; ag. treas., Dominica, 1928; warden, Northern dist. and mag., dist. C., 1928.

MOIR, WILLIAM JOHN, M.B., Ch.B. (Aberdeen), D.P.H. (Lond.), D.T.M. and H. (Eng.)—B. 1893; health offr., F.M.S., Nov., 1920; ditto, Kinta, Nov., 1925; ag. sr. health offr., N. Semiblan, Mar., 1928; sr. health offr., Johore, June, 1929; ag. prin. med. offr., Aug., 1932.

MOLLOY, PAUL AUGUSTUS, A.M.I.C.E., chartered civil engnr.—B. 1887; ed. King's Coll. Schl., Wimbledon and King's Coll., Lond.; asst. engnr., P.W.D., Madras, 1910-13; asst. engnr., P.W.D., F.M.S., Jan., 1913; asst. engnr., irrigation, F.M.S., May, 1915; exec. engnr., antimalarial br., Jan., 1922; exec. engnr., P.W.D., Nov., 1922; ag. sr. exec. engnr., in 1927 and 1931; senr. exec. engnr., P.W.D., S.S. and F.M.S., 1934.

MOLTENO, Hon. Sir James Tennant, K.T. Bach. (1911), B.A., LL.B., M.L.A.—B. 1865; ed. at Diocesan Coll., Rondebosch, and Trin. for native aff., Aug., 1896; transf. to Rhod. Coll., Camb.; called to the bar, Inner Temple; entd. Cape parlmt., 1890; speaker of Cape H. of A.; speaker of H. of A., Union of South Africa, 1910.

MONK, HAROLD FRANCIS, B.A. (Oxon.)—B. 1890; cadet, S.S., Nov., 1914; attd. censor's office Dec., 1914; attd. col. sec., Apr., 1917; asst. supt., govt. monop., Penang, July, 1926; offr. cl. III, Nov., 1926; ag. legal advr., Kedah, Jan., 1931; asst. advr., Nov., 1931; ag. advr., lands, Apr., 1932.

MONTAGNAC, LOUIS IVAN DE.—B. 1880; called to bar, Middle Temple, Jan., 1911; clk. of cts., parish of St. Andrew, Jamaica, May, 1921; ag. res. mag., St. Thomas, 1st Aug., 1922; ag. registr., sup. ct., Oct., 1924; registr., sup. ct., July, 1926.

MONTAGU, JAMES DROGO.—B. 1878; served, Cape Mounted Pol., 1903; Johannesburgh Mounted Pol., 1903-8; B.S.A. pol., 1908-9; S. Nigeria pol., 1909-18; local commt., Cyprus mily. pol., 24th Jan., 1920; ag. comnr., on various occasions in 1922-29 and 1932-33; ag. dep. ch. commdt., pol., June-Oct., 1925 and from Nov., 1926 to Feb., 1927; priv. sec. and A.D.C. to O.A.G., Oct. to Nov., 1926; ag. ch. commdt., pol. and inspr., prisons, July-Sept., 1928 and July to Sept., 1930; ag. Br. del. of Evcaf., July-Sept., 1930.

MONTGOMERY, H. R.—Asst. dist. comnr., E.A.P., May, 1908; dist. comnr., Apr., 1914; ag. senr. comnr., Kenya, 1926; senr. comnr., 2nd grade, 1929; 1st prov. comnr., 1932.

MOOD, H. L.—Asst. dist. comnr., E. Africa Prot., Feb., 1915; res. 2nd grade, Nyassaland, Nov., 1923; res. 1st grade, Mar., 1926; dist. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 1929.

MOODY, SYDNEY, O.B.E. (1932).—B. 1889; ed. King's Schl., Pontefract, Leeds Univ. and Lincoln Coll., Oxford (Hist. Schol.), 2nd cls. hist. finals, 1914; pte., Pub. Schla. Batt., R. Fusiliers, 1914; 2nd lieut., E. York. Regt., France, 1915; lieut., King's Liverpool Regt., Egypt, 1916; lieut., Herefordshire Regt., Palestine, 1917-1918; held various appts. in O.E.T.A. (S.) Palestine, Dec., 1918- June, 1920; dist. offr., Palestine, July, 1920; attd. to Middle East Dept., C.O., Feb., 1923 to Feb., 1924; asst. sec., 1924; ag. asst. ch. sec. and ch. sec. on various occasions, 1925-32.

MOONESINGHE, NALIN, B.A. (Oxon.)—Cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., May, 1924; attd., Anuradhapura kach., June, 1924; do., Batticaloa kach., Jan., 1925; do., Badulla kach., June, 1925; pol. mag., Pt. Pedro, Nov., 1926; ditto, Puttalam, May, 1927; ditto, Jaffna, Aug., 1929; office asst., Galle kach., Nov., 1930; pol. mag., Pt. Pedro, Nov., 1931; pol. mag., Jaffna, July, 1933.

MOOR, HERBERT WILLIAM.—B. 1891; obtained higher standard certif. in Forestry at Imperial Research Inst. and Coll., Dehra-Dun, India, 1914, with medals for forest engineering and sylviculture; probationer, Indian provincial forest service, 1914; passed exams. in Indian land revenue systems, forest law and accounts, and Hindustani by the higher standard, 1915; permanent extra asst. conservator, 1916; transf. to Trinidad as deputy conserv., forests, Jan., 1918; asst. conserv.. forests, Gold Coast, Jan., 1923; prin. forest offr., Apr., 1926.

MOOR, RICHARD, M.A. (Oxon.).—B. 1898; ed. Ernysted's Schl., Skipton and Hertford Col., Oxford; barrister-at-law, Middle Temple; cadet, S.S., July, 1921; asst. supt., govt. monop., S'pore., Mar., 1924; offr., cls. V, July, 1924; offr., cls. IV, July, 1928; sec. to res., Pahang, Nov., 1929; ag. solr.-gen., S.S., Sept., 1931 and Apr., 1932; dist. judge, S'pore., Penang and Malacca, Oct., 1932; ag. registr., sup. ct., Penang and offl. assignee in adnn., Nov., 1932; offr., cls. III, July, 1933.

MOORE, ERNEST STANLEY.—B. 1890; Imp. post office, 1909; war serv., Aug., 1914 to Mar., 1919; asst. survr., posts and tels., Nigeria, Sept., 1919; survr., do., 1926; divnl. survr., do., 1933.

MOORE, HENRY MONCK-MASON, C.M.G. (1930), B.A., Cantab.—B. 1887; cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1910; attd., col. sec.'s office, Dec., 1910; attd., Colombo kach., May, 1911; addtl. pol. mag., Colombo, Negombo and Avisawela, Aug., 1912; ditto, Colombo, and addtl. mun. mag., Colombo, Nov., 1912; office asst. to gov't. agt., Central Prov., Jan., 1913; office asst. to prin. collr., customs, and extra land survr., July, 1913; 4th asst. col. sec., Feb., 1914; 4th asst. col. sec., Oct., 1914; on mily. duty, May, 1916; addtl. asst. col. sec., July, 1919; 3rd asst. col. sec., Dec., 1919; 4th ditto, Jan., 1920; priv. sec. to offr. admstg. govt., Mar.-Sept., 1920, in adnn.; asst. gov't. agt., Trincomalee, Sept., 1920 to Dec., 1921; col. sec., Bermuda, Jan., 1922; prin. asst. sec., Nigeria, Jan., 1924; ag. dep. ch. sec. and ag. ch. sec. on various occasions, 1924-26; ag. ch. sec. to gov't., in 1926 and 1927; dep. ch. sec., Aug., 1927; gov't. dep., Sept. to Oct., 1927;
MOORE, Hon. Sir Newton James, K.C.M.G. (1910), C.M.G. (1908).—B. 1870; mayor of Bunbury, W. Aust., for some years, M.L.A. for Bunbury, 1904; min. of lands and agric., W. MOORE, Wilfred Henry, B.A. (Cantab.)—B. 1902; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1925; attd., Kalutara kach., Jan., 1926; ditto, Kandy kach., July, 1926; office ast., N'Elia kach., Jan., 1927; office ast., Ratnapura kach., May, 1928; do., Kandy kach., May, 1931; ast. govt. agt., Batticaloa, Dec., 1931.

MOORES-WEDDON, W. C.—B. 1880; ed. Dulwich and Trin. Coll., Dublin; cadet, B.N. Borneo, 1905; ast. dist. offr., 1906; offr. in-charge Tonom-Tawau expdn., 1906; dist. offr., 1908; ag. PLOWMAN, CLIFFORD HENRY FITZGERALD, O.B.E. (1928).—B. 1889; ed. at King's Schol., Ely and Trin. Coll., Camb.; B.A. (clasc. tripos); asst. dist. comanr., E. Consul on transfer Harar Consulate to C.O.; transf'd., Somaliland, 1922; H.B.M. chargé d'affaires, Addis Ababa, Dec., 1925 to Jan., 1926; 2nd cls., Star of Ethiopia; mem. mem. to Abyssinia or coronation of Emperor, 1928.

POLE-EVANS, LTDTD BULLER, C.M.G. (1921), M.A. (Cantab.), D.Sc. (Wales), F.L.S.—B. 1879; ed. Cowbridge Gram. Schl. and Univs. of Wales and Cambridge; mycologist, Transvaal, 1905; rep. African Assocn. for Advancement of Science, 1920; ch., divn. of botany, horticulture and entomology, 1927; ch., divn. of plant industry, 1929; author of many scientific papers.

POOLEY, CHARLES EDWARD.—B. 1903; apptd. after compet. exam., cler. offr., C.O., 22nd Oct., 1920; ag. cler. offr., higher grade, Aug., 1933.

POPE, GEORGE WILLIAM, L.L.M.R.C.P., and S.I. (Ireland), D.P.H., R.C.P. and S.I.—B. 1891; med. offr., Kenya, 1920; 2nd health offr., port med. dept., Hong Kong, 1924; ag. asst. bacteriologist, 1924; asst. health offr., 1925; health offr., 1926.

POPE, STEAD.—Br. post office, Feb., 1903; dist. survr., post and tels., Gold Coast, Dec., 1913; on activesserv., Togoland Field Force, Aug., 1914; and later in charge posts and tels., Togo-land to May, 1915; Imp. army serv., Sept., 1915-19; lieut., R.E. and R.A.F.; dist. survr., Gold Coast, June, 1919; div. survr., Jan., 1927; P.M.G., Nyasaaland, Mar., 1930.

POTTINGER, JOSEPH HECTOR, M.B., Ch.B., D.P.H., D.T.M. & H. (L'pool).—B. 1898; on war serv., 1915-18; med. offr., health, W. African med. staff, Gold Coast, 1928; astt. gov't. med. offr. of health, Br. Guiana, 1932.

POWELL, BASIL WELSTRADE BARNARD.—B. 1881; ed. George Watson's Coll., Edin. and Highfield Coll., Southampton; senr. engr., P. and T. dept., S.S. and F.M.S., Penang, Mar., 1913; ditto, K. Lumpur, July, 1923; ditto, N. Sembilan, Dec., 1923.

ROSEDALE, JOHN LEWIS, Ph.D. (Bonn), D.Sc. (Aberdeen), F.I.C.—B. 1889; prof. of biochemistry, King Edward VII Medical Coll., Singapore, Apr., 1927; off. deleg. to 8th cong. of Far Eastern Assn. of Trop. Med., Bangkok, Dec., 1930.

ROSEDALE, WILLIAM ORIEL PELLY.—B.1891; astt. dist. offr., Nigeria, Aug., 1914; dist. offr., 1924; astt. sec. and clk., exec. and leg. couns., 1927; ag. prin. astt. sec., 1930-31; admstve. offr., class I., Oct., 1930.

ROSENOW, JACOBUS DANIEL MALAN, B.A., LL.B.—B. 1884; ed. Boys' Public Schl., Rondelosch; Cape civ. serv., audit office, Capetown, 1903; atty. gen's. office, Capetown, 1907, various mag. offices for 12 years; clk., office of dir., prisons, 1922; jun. prof. astt. att. gen., Natal, 1923; regisr., high ct. ROSS, EDWARD ANDREW, M.C.—B. 1895; ed. Leigh Gram. Schl. and Manchester Univ.; on active serv., 1914-19; relinquished comm., 1921 with rank of capt.; cadet, F.M.S., May, 1920; passed cadet, Dec., 1921; supernumry offr., cls. V, May, 1923; astt. contrlr., lab., Penang, Mar., 1925; offr., cls. Patatand mag., Klang, Jan., 1928; astt. advr., Kukup, Sept., 1928; contrlr., lab., Johore, Jan., 1930; offr., cls. III, May, 1932.

ROSS, GEORGE ARCHIBALD PARK, M.D., Ch.M. (Edin.), D.P.H. (Edin.); diploma, trop. diseases, Liverpool.—B. 1879; S. ROSS, J. G. H.—Astt. dist. commr., E.A.P., Sept., 1919; ag. junr. astt. sec., Kenya, Nov., 1919 to Oct., 1919; ag. clk. of exec. and leg. couns., Dec., 1919 to Mar., 1920; editor, offl. Gazette, Feb., 1920 to Mar., 1920.

ROSS, JAMES SANDFORD.—B. 1884; ed. Merchant Taylors Schl.; mily. serv., 1914-19; N.W. Frontier campaign, 1915; Salonica Field Force, 1916-19; astt. treas., Kenya, 1919.

ROSS, OSWALD F.—Ed. Malvern Coll. and Jesus Coll., Cambridge; capt., N. Staffs. Regt., European War; served Dardanelles expdn., 1915; Mesopotamia, 1916; passed A.T.S. course, 1920; astt. dist. commr. Gold Coast, 1920.

ROUSE, HAROLD STUART, C.E., A.M.I.C.E.—B. 1888; ed. Truro Coll. and Christ's Hosp.; survr., P.W.D., Hong Kong, Feb., 1912; engrnr., drainage wks. office, Dec., 1913; transf. to gen. wks. office, P.W.D., Apr., 1915; ag. exec. engrnr., G.W.O., Sept., 1915-16 and from Feb., 1921 to Oct., 1922; offr. in charge, G.W.O., May, 1924; sec., water emergency comtee., May to Aug., 1929; exec. engrnr., roads office, P.W.D., Nov., 1931.

ROWAN, WILLIAM ALFRD.—B. and educ. Graaff Reinet, Cape Prov.; civ. serv., lower, 1903; higher, 1907; LL.B., 1921; Rhodesian pol., 1897; O.R.C. pol., 1900; astt. mag., O.F.S., 1905; addnl. mag., Bloemfontein, 1915; overseas mily. serv., 1916-20; ret. as capt.; ment. in desps.; mag., Senekal, 1920; addnl. mag., Pretoria, 1920; mag., Bethlehem and Kroonstad, 1928; do., Port Elizabeth, 1932.

ROWATT, HUGH HOWARD.—B. 1861; ed., Ottawa Coll. Inst. and St. Catherine's Affiliated Coll.; ent. civ. serv., Can.,1887, as correspondent; ch. clk., minin., lands br., Mar., 1907; contr., mining lands, 1912; supt., 1920; mem., Dominion lands bd., 1928; dep. min. of interior, 1931.

ROWE, CHARLES HAWKSWELL.—B. 1885; astt. acct., constrn., F.M.S. Railways, Feb., 1912; divisl. acct., June, 1913-Jly., 1914; acct. and audr., constrn., head office, Kuala Lumpur, Mar., 1920; stores supt., F.M.S. Rlys., Nov., 1926.

ROWE, ERIC GEORGE.—B. 1904; ed. Chatham House Schl., Ramsgate and St. Edmund Hall, Oxford; B.A. 1926; cadet, Tanganyika Territory, 1928; astt. dist. offr., 1930.

ROWE, GEORGE FREDERICK.—B. 1878; ent. Crown Agent's office, 1896; astt. head, stores dept., 1917; astt. head, pay dept., 1920; cashier, 1921; dep. head, finance dept., 1927; dep. head, stores dept., 1929; dep. head, finance dept., 1932; head, pay dept., 1933.

ROWE, LIEUT.-COL. R. H., D.S.O., M.C.—B. 1883; ed. Wellington Coll. and Royal Mily. Acad., Woolwich; Royal Art'y., 1902-25; Bermuda and Jamaica, 1902-6; served with native infantry, Nigeria, 1907-10; Northern Hinterland exped., 1907-8; Niger Cross River exped., 1908-9; operations against Abini, 1909, and against Munichis, 1910; dep. dir., surveys, Nigeria, 1911; Nigeria-Dahomey bndry. commr. 1912; Great war (Cameroons, France and Russia), 1914-18; survr.gen., Gold Coast, 1920; commr., lands, in addn., 1924; survr.-gen., Sierra Leone, in addn., 1925; Gold Coast rep. with staff of H.R.H. the Prince of Wales on his visit to W. Africa, 1925; chmn., comtees. on pub. wks. accts., rly. constrn., munici. finance and mily. defence; mem., leg. coun., 1926; astmstve, serv., staff grade, Nigeria, Oct., 1926; commr., lands, chmn., Lagos development bd., regist., companies, offl. recr., M.L.C. 1933.
ROWELL, THOMAS, B.Sc. (Hon.), Dipl. in Educat., Liverpool Univ.—B. 1896; ed. Douglas Secondary Sch., and Univ. of Liverpool Training Coll.; war serv., 1915-1918; mast. educan., dep., Hong Kong, Mar., 1923.

ROWELL, THOMAS HUBERT.—Clk., loco. dept., I.M.R., Pretoria, Oct., 1900; acotg. brch., ch. loco. sup'ts office, Jan., 1903; acotg. offr., ch. mech. engrn. dept., July, 1908; inspr., audit dept., S.A.R. and Harbrs., Oct., 1910; inspr., asst. contr. and audr. gen.'s dept., Union of S. Africa, May, 1911; inspr., (ryls. and hbrs.) control and audit dept., July, 1916; senr. inspr., (ryls. and harbrs.) control and audit dept., Oct., 1922; ch. inspr. (ryls. and harbrs.) control and audit dept., Apr., 1933.

ROWEN, F. C. P.—B. 1896; copyist, audit dept., B. Honduras, 1912; 3rd cls. clk., atty.-gen.'s off., 1915; 2nd cls. clk., ditto, 1918; clk. to regar.-gen., 1919; sec., riot enquiry comm., 1919; ag. regar.-gen. and cust. enemy ppty. and contr. local clearing office, 1920; sec., yellow fever enquiry comm., 1921; again ag. regar. gen., 1921, 1923 and 1925; regar.-gen., regar., lands titles, regar., sup., vice-admry. and bankcy., cts., regar., companies and patents and regar., births marriages and deaths, 1927; J.P.; stamp comsnr., dir., pub. offrs. guarantee fund; comsnr., income tax, 1927.

RUNDLE, GEN. SIR HENRY MACLEOD LESLIE, R.A.—B. 1856; G.C.B. (1911); G.C.M.G. (1914); G.C.V.O. (1911); K.C.B., 1898; K.C.M.G., 1901; D.S.O., 1897; ed. Roy. Mil. Acad., Woolwich; entd. Comd., 1905-7; col.-comdt., R.A., 1907; gov. and comdr.-in-chief Malta, 1909-1915.

RUSHTON, CHARLES BERKELLEY, I.S.O. (1931).—Clk., comsnr. of ryls. dept., W. Aust., Apr., 1896; ch. clk., July, 1896; ag. sec. to comanr. of ryln., 23rd Aug., 1901; sec. to ditto, 18th Dee., 1901; sec., W. Australian London Agency, 3rd Nov., 1919.

RUSHTON, HERBERT HARVEY, C.B.E. (1934).—B. 1876; acot., electric light dept., Gibraltar, 1897; asst. sec. and asst. acct., munic. authority, 1902; ch. acct. and asst. sec., 1903; sec. and finan. offr., 1908 (also man., pub. electricity and water supplies, mem., comttee, on exchange and currency); asst. ch. acct., Uganda Rly., E. Africa Prot., 1915; lieut., E.A. Forces, 1915; capt., 1916; ag. dep. ch. acct., Uganda Rly., 1916 to June, 919 (also govt. rep., Nairobi munic. coun., 1918, mem., gen. manager's advisory comttee., 1919); dep. treas., Kenya Colony, 1920 and 1921; ag. treas., Aug., 1920 to Apr., 1921; mem., exec. and leg. couns. (also chmn., currency and other comttees); col. treas., Fiji, 1922 (with charge of group of depts., cust., port and marine, transport, posts, telegraphs and telephones, govt. stores, and returned soldiers' dairy sttlmt.); mem., exec. and leg. couns.; comanr. of currency, mem., educan., mining and other bds.; chmn., many comttees.; ag. col. sec., Apr., 1929; gov.'s dep. for four periods; treas., Kenya, Mar., 1930.

RUSSELL, MAJOR-GEN. SIR ANDREW HAMILTON.—K.C.B. 1918; K.C.M.G. (1915).—B. 1868; held comanr. as lieut. for 5 yrs. in Imperial Army; vol. offr., New Zealand, 1900; tea. A.D.C. to H.E. the Gov. of N.Z., 1911; brig.-gen., 1914; temp. major-gen., 1915; major-gen., in command of N.Z. Div., 1916.

RUSSELL, WILLIAM, M.D.—B. 1888; ed. Univ.; Union of S. Africa mental hosp. serv., 1913; comsnr., mental hygiene, 1922.

RUSSELL, SIR WILLIAM ALISON, Kt. Bath (1928), K.C.—B. 1875; ed. Rugby and Trin. Coll. Camb.; B.A., LL.B., honours, 1897; barrister-at-law, Inner Temp., 1900; eqy. bar, 1900-6; apptd. Crown advoc., pub. procr., admstr. gen., prin. regar. of docuta. rec'd. of companies, Uganda Prot., May, 1906; Crown advoc. and pub. procr., Jan., 1908; ch. chief sec. to govt., Aug., 1909, to Mar., 1916; Crown advoc. and pub. procr., Mar. to May, 1910; ag. chief sec. to govt., June, 1910 to May, 1911; Crown advoc. and pub. procr., June, 1911 to June, 1912; King's advoc., Cyprus, July, 1912; mem. of exec. and legis. couns., 1912; joint comanr. under Reprint of Statutes Law, 1912; edition publ., Feb., 1914; K.C., Cyprus, 1924; ch. just., Tanganyika Territory, 1924; ret. and re-apptd. as legal advr. to govt. of Malta, 1924; published, "Legislative and other Forms" (2nd edn. 1928) and "Handbook for Magistrates" (2nd edn., 1928).

RUSSELL, WILLIAM HAYWORTH.—B. 1894; clk., Mankainana, Swaziland, Apr., 1915; clk., treas., 1920; asst. acct. and asst. coll., inc. tax, 1922; acot., 1928; ag. finan. sec., Apr. to Oct., 1931.

RUSSELL, W. J., A.I.M.M.—Ed. Royal Coll. of Science, Ireland and Cornwall Cent. Schol. of Mining; asst. inspr., mines, Nigeria, 1914; inspr., mines, 1919; ag. dep. ch. inspr., 1923; 1923, 1926 and 1928; dep. ch. inspr., mines, 1929; ag. ch. inspr., mines, 1930.

RUTHERFOORD, JOHN WINNE CORNELL, B.A. (Oxon).—B. 1888; ed. St. Paul's Schol. and Merton Coll., Oxford; asst. dist. comanr., S. Nigeria, 1911; seconded as asst. recr., 1914; sec., Nigerian secretariat, Lagos, 1926; clk. exec. and leg. couns., 1926; cl. i., grade i., admn. serv., 1928.

RUTHERFORD, CAPT. PETER WILLIAM, M.C. (1916), F.R.G.S.—B. 1894; ed. Brighton Coll.; 2nd lieut., W. Yorks Regt., 1914; lieut., 1915; seconded, Flying Corps, 1916; capt., 1917; ret. from army, 1919; asst. dist. comanr., G. Coast, Sept., 1921.

RYCKMAN, HON. EDMOND BAIRD, R.A., M.A., LL.B., K.C.—B. 1866; ed. Bradford Colleg. Inst., Toronto Univ. and Osgoode Hall; el. to H. of C., Canada, 1921; re-el., 1925; min. of pub. wks. in Meighen Cabinet, 1926; re-el. g.e., 1928; min. of national rev. in Bennett cabinet, 1930.

RYRIE, MAJ.-GEN. HON. SIR GRANTVILLE DE LAUNE, K.C.M.G. (1919), C.B. (1918), C.M.G. (1916), V.D.—B. 1865; ed. King's Schil. Parramatta; mem., state parl., N.S.W., 3 years mem., house of reps., C. of A., 1911-27; asst. min. for defence, 1919-22; commanded 3rd Light Horse Regt., N.S.W., for 7 yrs. with rank of lieut.-col.; served S. Africa, 1900-01 (severely wounded (Queen's med. 4 clasps); European War, 1914-18; commanded 2nd Light Horse Brig., A.I.F., Egypt; commanded Australian divn., Syria; G.O.C., Australian Force, Kt., (wounded twice, five times ment. in des.) maj.-gen. commdg., 1st Cav. Divn., N.S.W., 1923-27; high comanr. for Australia, 1927-32.
SAINT, SYDNEY JOHN, B.Sc., A.I.C.—B.1897; ed. Beaumaris Grammar Sch.; Reading Univ.; B.Sc., 1920; served with R.A.F., 1916-19; Salter research fellow, 1920-22; lect. in agrl. chemistry, Leeds Univ., 1922-26; agrl. chemist, Barbados, 1927.

ST. JOHNSTON, LIEUT.-COL. SIR REGINALD, K.O.M.G. (1931), C.M.G. (1923), Barrister-at-law (Middle Temple); M.R.C.S., L.R.C.P., Lond., etc.—Ed. Queen Elizabeth Coll., Guernsey and Cheltenham Coll.; various appts. in home civ. service; entered Fiji civ. serv., 1907; commr. Lau Islands, 1909; seconded for European war; D.A.D.M.S., B.E.F., France; subsequently attached to W.O. (brevet lieut.-col. and recd. thanks of S.O.), col. sec., Falkland Is., Dec. 1918; ag. gov., Falkland Is., from Sept. 1919 to Apr., 1920; col. sec., Leeward Islds., Dec., 1919; ag. gov., Leeward Is., eight times; admstr. govt. of Antigua on many occasions; ag. admstr., Dominica, 1925; admstr., St. Kitts-Nevis, 9th May 1926; assumed duty, 23rd Nov., 1926; gov., Leeward Is., Sept., 1929; author of "The Lau Islands, Fiji," "The Children of the Sun," "The Falkland Islands," "The Islanders of the Pacific," "South Sea Reminiscences," "West Indian Talus" and some novels, etc.

SALE, GILBERT NOEL, B.Sc. (Forestry, Edin.)—B. 1897; ed. King Alfred's Sch., Wantage, Edinburgh Univ. and Imp. Forestry Inst., Oxford; army serv., 1916-19; lieut., R.A. (S.R.); astt. conserv. forests, Cyprus, Mar., 1922; ag. astt. prin. forest offr., 1924; ag. prin. forest offr., 1926-28; dir., forests, Mauritius, Dec., 1928; conserv., forests, July, 1930.

SALMON, FREDERICK JOHN, M.C., A.C.G.I., F.R.G.S., Lieut.-Col., R. of O., R.E.—B. 1882; ed. Univ. Coll. Schil., Lond., and Cent. Tech. Coll., S. Kensington; empid. on Transvaal Mines, 1904-1907; assoc., inst. of mining and metallurgy; astt. supt., surveys, Ceylon, June, 1908; supt., surveys, 1914; served with field survey units in France, 1915-19; thrice ment. in desps.; lieut.-col., supt., surveys, on staff (appl. surveys), Ceylon, 1924; ag. astt. surv. gen., 1928; dir., land registrn., and surveys, Cyprus, Sept., 1930; offr. commdg. sp. constab., 1932; dir., surveys, Palestine, 1933.

SALOMONE, WALTER.—B. 1888; ed. St. Ignatius Coll. and Malta Univ.; elec. for 6th divn. in leg. assem., Oct., 1921; re-elec., June, 1924 and Aug., 1927; min. for industry and commerce, Aug., 1927.

SAMARAKOON, EDWIN RICHARD DEALWIS.—B. 1877; cls. V. Ceylon civ. serv., Oct., 1927; extra office astt., Badulla kach., Oct., 1927; office astt. to contr., rev., Feb., 1928; office astt. to land commr., July, 1931.

SAMARASINGHE, SOLOMON DIAS.—B. 1875; cls. V Ceylon civ. serv., May, 1929; extra office astt., Kurunegala kach., May, 1929.

SAMBIDGE, GERALD CHURCHILL.—B. 1886; ed. King Edward's Sch., Birmingham; served Nigeria Regt., Mar., 1915; instr. in arts and crafts, N. Provs., Nigeria, Dec., 1920.

SAMPSON, BASIL FEHRSEN, M.C.—B. 1888; ed. St. Andrew's Coll., Grahamstown; M.B., B.S., Lond. Univ. (Guy's Hosp.), 1917; M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), 1915; temp. surg., R.N. (H.M.S. Benbow), 1915; tempy. capt., S.A.M.C., France, 1916; M.C., 1918; astt. bacteriologist, Guy's Hosp.; senr. govt. pathologist, Union of S. Africa health dept., Durban, 1931.

SAMPSON, HON. HENRY WILLIAM, O.B.E. (1918).—B. 1872; mem., Transvaal parlmt., 1907-10; mem., Union parlmt., 1910-33; joined Union cabinet as min. for posts and tels. and pub. wks., Nov., 1928-Mar., 1933; pres., S.A. typographical union, 1903-1929.

SAMUEL, Rt. Hon. Sir HERBERT LOUIS, P.C. (1908), G.B.E. (1920), M.A.—B. 1870; ed. University Coll. Schil. and Balliol Coll., Oxford; M.P., Cleveland Divn., N. Riding, Yorks., 1902-18; partly under sec., home dept., 1905-9; chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster (with a seat in the cabinet), 1909-10 and 1915-16; P.M.G., 1910-14 and 1915-16; pres. of the L.G.B., 1914-15; sec. of state for home affairs, 1916; chmn. of the select comte. of house of commons on national expenditure, 1917-18; British sp. commr. to Belgium, 1919; grand offr. of the Order of Leopold of Belgium, 1919; high commr., Palestine, 1920-25.

SAMUEL, SILVERIC I., M.B.E. (1924).—Ed. at St. Gregory's Rom. Cath. gram. schil., Lagos; measr. and copyt., educ. off., Oct., 1897; clk. to inspr. of schils., Mar., 1899; sec. to comte. for exhibtn. of schil. wks., 1902 and 1903; clk. and interpreter to trav. commr., Ilesha, interior dept., Feb., 1904; 3rd cls. clk., govt.'s off., Aug., 1904; conf. clk. to the gov. of Nigeria.

SANDERS, JOHN OWEN, A.M.I.C.E.—B. 1892; ed. Elstow Schil. and Manchester Univ.; mil. ser., 1916-20; 2nd lieut., 1917; ag. capt., 1918; astt., Crewe loco. works, L.M.S.R., 1922; works man., F.M.S. Rlys., 1924; run. supt., 1927; ag. traffic man., Aug., 1930; transportation man., 1932.

SANDERSON, I., M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.), D.T.M., D.T.H. (Liv.)—B. 1894; mily. serv., 1914-19; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, 1925.

SANDFORD, GEORGE RITCHIE, O.B.E. (1924), Barrister-at-Law, Inner Temple, 1924.—Astt. dist. commr., E. Africa Prot., Feb., 1915; priv. sec. to gov., 1918; junr. astt. sec. and clk. of couns., Sept., 1922; ag. senr. astt. sec., Mar. to Sept., 1923; resig., 1925; clk. to leg. coun., Jan., 1926; edr., official gazette, Mar., 1926; dep. treas., 1931.

SANDFORD, THOMAS FREDERICK, M.R.E., B.A.—B. 1886; ed. Marlborough Coll. and Oriel Coll., Oxford; astt. native commr., N. Rhodesia, Sept., 1910; native commr., Apr., 1913; served in E. SANGER-DAVIES, ARTHUR ELPHINSTONE.—B. 1888; ed. SANSOM, CHARLES HENRY.—B. 1886; ed. Plymouth and Munnahmed Coll.; barrister-at-law, Middle Temple, 1923; pol. probationer, 1905; regisr. of criminals, F.M.S. and S.S., 1910; asst. comsrr. of pol., Ipoh, 1911; adjt., F.M.S. pol., 1913; comsrr. of pol., Johore, 1921; supt. pol., S'pore but cont. former appt., Nov., 1924; ch. pol. offr., S'pore, Dec., 1929; offg. ch. pol. offr., Perak, Nov., 1930; comsrr., pol., F.M.S., Oct., 1931.

SARGENT, CARR R. G., M.B.E. (1928), A.I.N.A., F.R.G.S.—Port offr., Kenya, Jan., 1917; port capt., 1926.

African War, 1899-1902; col. representative on Zululand Lands Delimitation Coms., 1902, and comsrr. for native affairs, 1905; ret., 1909.

SAUNDERS, PHILLIP HENRY NORMAN.—B. 1890; ed. Queen's Coll., Br. Guiana; successively 6th, 5th, 4th, 3rd and 2nd cls. clk., P.W.D., Br. Guiana, 1911-24; sec., bd. of industrial training, 1930; acctg. clk., P.W.D., 1931; sec., advisory comttee, on sea defences, 1932; sec., sea defence bd., 1933.

SAUNDERS-JONES, DAVID WILLOUGHBY.—B. 1899; ed. SAUVE, HON. ARTHUR, P.C. (Can.).—B. 1875; ed. Seminary of Ste. Therese and L'Univ. de Montreal; 1st cl. to legis. assem., Quebec, g.e., 1908; re-elec., g.e., 1912, 1916, 1919, 1923 and 1927; el. to H. of C., Canada, g.e., 1930; P.M.G., in Bennett Cabinet, 1930; re-elec. by accl. after assuming office, Aug., 1930.

SAVAGE, GEORGE.—B. 1887; supt. of regis-trn., G.P.O., Singapore, Oct., 1914; supt. of mails, ditto, Jan., 1915; supt. mails, Penang, but cont. ag. snr. supt. mails, July, 1917; supt., grade II., Jan., 1919; supt., grade I., Jan., 1920; supt., posts and teles., Malacca, Sept., 1920; senr. acct., G.P.O., S'pore., contd. to act as contr., P. and T., Jan., 1929; contr., P. and T., F.M.S., Aug., 1929; ag. P.M.G., Sept., 1929; P.M.G., Johore, July, 1930.

SAVARY, JOHN LEWIS HENRY WILLIAM.—B. 1884; col. schol., Trinidad, 1901; Gray's Inn, 1902; prizeman in evidence, procedure and criminal law exam., 1904; barrister-at-law, Nov., 1905; practised at bar, Trinidad, 1906-24; retainer from Trinidad govt. as junr. coun. to atty-gen., Jan., 1916-Dec., 1923; ag. solr.-gen., in 1921, 1922 and 1923; regisr. and marshal and regis-r. gen. and prin. regisr., West Indian ct. of appeal, Jan., 1925; ag. puisne judge in 1925 and 1926; puisne judge, Br. Guiana, 1928.

SAVI, VICTOR GEORGE.—B. 1884; pol. probationer, S.S., Nov., 1904; asst. supt pol. Jal., 1908; asst. supt of pol., Penang, Oct., 1917; dir., crim. intell., Jan., 1920; dep. comsrr., pol., Perak, Mar., 1922; supt., pol., S'pore., Oct., 1922.

SAVILE, ARTHUR HUGH, Dip. Agr. (Wye, A.I.C.T.A.—B. 1908; ed. Clifton Coll., Wye Agr. Coll. and C.O. Sch., course Oxford and Trinidad; dist. agril. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Oct., 1928.

SAWARD, CAPT. SIDNEY CARMON, M.C. (1916), M.M. (1916).—B. 1889; fellow of surveyors inst.; served with 509 (1-1) Lond. Field Coy., R.E., 6th divn.; home serv., Aug. to Dec., 1914; France and Germany, Dec., 1914 to June, 1919; Ire and June to Aug., 1919; commdg., cadre, 12th Field Coy., R.E.; commd., Sept., 1913; lieut., June, 1916; capt., Oct., 1918; ag. major, Dec., 1918 to Jan., 1919; ment. in desps., Mar., 1919; surr., field Coast, Nov., 1919; field supervisor Apr., 1924; ag. dep. survr.-gen. on various occasions, 1923-32; ag. survr.-gen., Feb.-June, 1927; asst. survr.-gen., Apr., 1929.

SAWTELL, WILLIAM GEORGE.—B. 1894; ed. at King Edward VI's Sch., Bath, and H.M.S. "Worcester"; H.M. Transport Serv., 1913-17; Indian govt. tel. ship, 1917-18; Indian Army R. of O., 1918-22; wharf-mast. and pilot, Tanganyika Territory, 1922; marine offr., 1932.

SAXTON, SIDNEY WARING.—Ed. Toulouse (France), and Dean Close Schl., Cheltenham; paymr. cadet, R.N., July, 1905; paymr. hout. comdr., Mar., 1918; 1st cls. French interpreter, lent to C.O. and apptd. asst. dist. comsrr. G. Coast, Sept., 1914, but did not take up apptm., having resumed duty in H.M. Navy for the period of the war; assumed duties as junr. asst. col. sec., G. Coast, Apr., 1919; ag. asst. col. sec., May, 1919; ag. dist. comsrr., Accra, and ag. trav. comsrr. for Accra-Akwapim and Birrim dists., Oct., 1919; invalided, H.M. Navy, 1920; passed Tropical African service course (all subjects, 2nd part); barrister-at-law, Middle Temple, 1925; promoted pay comdr., ret. list, 1927; dep. prov. comsrr., 1930.

SAYER, GEOFFREY ROBLEY, B.A.—B. 1887; ed. at Highgate schl. (founder) and Queen's Coll., Oxford; open exhib. in classics and Fitzgerald exhibr.; 2nd cls. class. mods.; 3rd cls. lit. hum. (B.A., 1910); cadet, Hong Kong, Oct., 1910; passed in Cantonese, Nov., 1912; ag. asst. dist. offr. (South), 1912 to 1913; ag. asst. supt. pol., 1913 to 1914; ag. dep. offr. recvr., 1914 to 1915; ag. ch. asst. sec. for Chinese affrs. 1914 and 1915, in addn. to other duties; priv. sec. to gov., in addn. 1915; attd. to crown solr.'s off., 1915; passed final exam. in Hakka, July, 1915; ag. chief asst. sec. for Chinese affrs., 1915; miliy. serv., 1915-19; dep. regist. and apprais. Hong Kong, 1920; head, army. dept., 1920;
passed in Mandarin, May, 1921; attd. to treasy, 1924; asst. treas. and comsrr. of estate duties, Apr., 1925; supt., impts. and expts. dept., June, 1927; P.M.G., Apr., 1928; head, sany. dept., Oct., 1928.

SAYERS, ELDER FRANK.—B. 1889; ed. King's Coll. Schl., Wimbledon, St. John's Coll., Cambridge, and Grenoble Univ., B.A., LL.B. (Cantab.); barrister-at-law (Inner Temple), Apr., 1913; passed lower and higher stand. exams. in Temne, and lower stand. exam. in Koranko; war service, E. Africa, 1918; asst. dist. comsrr., Sierra Leone, Jan., 1915; dist. comsrr., Aug., 1922.

SAYERS, FREDERICK RICHARDSON.—B.A., B.C., B.A.O., M.D., D.P.H. (Dublin Univ.)—B. 1880; ed. Rathmines Schl., Dublin, The Meath Hosp., Dublin, and Trin. Coll., Dublin; res. med. offr., Monkstown Hosp., Dublin, 1909-12; med. offr., S.S., Mar., 1912; med. offr., gen. hosp., Penang, Apr., 1912; port health offr. Penang, and med. offr. in ch. of leper asylum, Pulau Jerejak, Penang, Sept., 1912; asst. censor, Penang, in addition, Sept., 1914, to Apr., 1916; lecturer in hygiene, King Edward VII. medical schl., S'pore, 1919, 1923, 1926 and 1928; senr. health offr., Penang, Feb., 1924; ols., B., Jan., 1925; mem., Br. delegation to internat. sany. conf. Paris, 1926; senr. health offr., Perak, Feb., 1927; ch. health offr., S'pore, May, 1928; regiar. gen., births and deaths, S.S., Jan., 1931.

SAYERS, GERALD FLEMING.—B. 1893; ed. Westminster and Christ Church, Oxford; B.A. (hons.) 1914; asst. dist. comsrr., E. Africa Prot., Feb., 1915; ag. senr. asst. sec., Nov., 1919 to July, 1920; asst. sec., Tanganyika territory, July, 1920; ag. senr. asst. sec., for various periods 1920-24; clk. to exec. coun., Sept., 1923; attd. to C.O., Aug., 1924 to Sept., 1925 and from July to Sept., 1930; clk., leg. coun., 1926-32; ag. asst. ch. sec., on various occasions, 1927-1931; asst. ch. sec., 1932; asst. ch. sec., Nyasaland Prot., 1933; edr., Handbook of Tanganyika Territory, 1930.

SAYLE, LIEUT. COMMDR., ARTHUR REGINALD WILLIS, R.N.R., Barrister-at-Law (Gray's Inn).—Ed. Merchant Taylors Schl. and cadet H.M.S. "Worcester"; Royal Navy, May, 1914; R.I.C., 1920; admstrv. offr., S. Nigeria, May, 1921; station mag., Ibadan, S. Nigeria, Aug., 1925; pol. mag., Oct., 1928; crown coun., 1930; ag. solr. gen., in 1932 and 1933.

SCADDAN, HON. JOHN, C.M.G. (1924), M.L.A.—B. 1876; leader of Parly. Lab. party in W. Aust. since Aug., 1910; elected for Ivanhoe, June, 1904; premier of W. Australia, 1911-1916, min. for rly., mines and industry, 1930.

SCAMMELL, ERNEST HENRY.—B. 1873; ed. privately; sec. various business concerns, 1891-1907; visited Australia, engaged in business and journalism in Canada, 1907-1913; organizing sec., Canadian Peace Centenary Association, under the auspices of the govt. of Canada, 1913; asst. cable censor, dept. of militia and defence, Canada, 1915; sec., mil. hosps. coman., Canada, 1915; asst. dep. min. and sec., dept. of soldiers' civil re-establish., Canada, 1918; negotiated reciprocal agreements between Canadian, British and United States Govts., regarding treatment and training of Naval and Military Forces resident in these countries, 1919; sec., pensions divn., dept. of pensions and national health, 1931; Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Secretaries (London); Fellow of the Royal Colonial Institute (London); mem. of the Exec. of the Canadian Peace Centenary Assoc.

SCHARFF, JOHN WILLIAM, B.A., M.D., B.A.O., B.Ch., D.P.H. (T.C.), D.T.M. & H. (Lond.).—B. 1895; surgn. sub.-lieut., R.N.V.R., July, 1915; health offr., S.S., Nov., 1920; lect. in biology, King Edward VII Coll. of Medicine in addn., May, 1921; hon. sec. for Malaya of the Far Eastn. Assoc. of Trop. Med., Aug., 1921; health offr., Malacca, June, 1925; sr. health offr., Penang, May, 1928; offl. deleg. to 8th cong. of Far Eastn. Assoc. of Trop. Med., Bangkok, Dec., 1930.

SCHMIDT, CARL FRIEDRICH, B.A.—Civ. serv. law clk., law dept., Cape, May, 1893; control and audit office, July, 1893; asst. examnr. of accts., Jan., 1894; examnr., May, 1898; ch. examnr., July, 1907; inspr. of accts., Jan., 1909; prin. clk., Apr., 1912; sec. educn. dept., Bloemfontein, 16th Aug., 1915; ag. dir. of educn., O.F.S., July, 1918; dir. of educn., O.F.S., June, 1920; sec. for interior, Sept., 1926; contr. and audr.-gen., 1929.

SCHNEIDER, SIR GALUTHERUS STEWART, Kt. Bach. (1928), K.C.—B. 1864; ag. puisne just., Ceylon, Jan., 1921; comsrr. of assize, Nov., 1921; puisne just., Dec., 1921; ag. ch. just., Sept.-Dec., 1926; ret.

SCHOC, AUGUST ARNOLD.—B. 1883; ed. Berne, Switzerland; graduated, Leiden, LL.D. and called to bar, Middle Temple, 1910; ent. Union pub. serv., 1911; priv. sec. to min. of justice, 1913-16; professional asst. to atty.-gen. (Transvaal), 1916-24; solr.-gen., Cape Eastern Dists., Aug., 1924; law adviser and Dutch draughtsman, dept. of just., Pretoria, Sept., 1925; senr. law adviser, Oct., 1931.

SCHOFIELD, WALTER.—B. 1888; ed. Univ. of Liverpool, M.A.; non-coll. student, Oxford, 1908-1911, M.A.; cadet, Hong Kong, Nov., 1911; attached to secretariat for Chinese affairs, 1914; asst. cable censor, in addition to other duties, 1914 to 1915; passed cadet, Feb., 1915; ag. 3rd asst. to sec. for Chinese affairs, 1915; ag. 2nd ditto on various occasions, 1915-23; passed law exam., 1916; ag. dep. regiar. and appraiser, in addn. to other duties, 1919; ag. chief asst. to sec. for Chinese affrs, in 1919, 1920 and 1921; dist. offr., South, in addn., 1922; dist. offr., South, 1923; mag., Hong Kong, 1926; mag., Kowloon, 1927; asst. supt., impts. and expts., 1929-30; dist. offr., South, 1930; 1st pol. mag., 1931.

SCHOKMAN, CLIVE CONRADE.—B. 1897; 4th supt., prisons, Ceylon, Jan., 1924; 1st do., Apr., 1928; ag. inspr.-gen., prisons, Dec., 1931.

SCHOLEFIELD, GUY HARDY, D.Sc. (Lond.), O.B.E. (1919).—Ed. Tokomairiro High. Schl. and Univ. of N.Z. (Bowen and Macmillan Brown prizeman) and Univ. of London; ch. librarian, gen. assembly liby. and contrlr., dominion archives, N.Z., 1926.

SCHOLEFIELD, WILLIAM.—Dep. clk., res. mag.s. ct., Jamaica, Mar., 1913; clk., res. mag.s. ct., Feb., 1917; asst. comsrr. and mag. Turks and Caicos Islands, July, 1919; ag. comsrr., ditto, Sept. to Oct., 1920; ag. res. mag., Jamaica, on various occasions, 1922-26.

SCIULUNA, HANNIBAL P., L.P.—B. 1880; ed. St. Ignatius' Coll., Malta; matric., Malta Univ., 1897; ent. Malta civ. serv., 1902; legal procurator, 1905; sec. and regiar., Malta Univ., 1913-20; rep. of govt. emigrn. dept. in devastated regions, France, 1920; attd., ministry of justice, 1921; esquire, Order of St. John of Jerusalem.
(Rome), 1910; Officier d'Academie (France), 1921; mem. of the Societe Academique d'Histoire Internationale de Paris, 1923; librn., Malta public library, July, 1923.

SCOTT, ERIC ELEANOR.—Ent. C.O. as typist, July, 1913; shorthand writer, Aug., 1918; cler. offr., 9th Mar., 1922.

SCOTT, ECSTACE LINDSAY, C.M.G. (1933), O.B.E. (1918), M.C. (1917).—B. 1885; ed. Bradford, and Univ. Coll., Oxford, B.A., 1908; asst. dist. comsrr., Uganda, Dec., 1908; dist. comsrr., June, 1918; seconded for mily. serr., 1914-19; dep. asst. dir., transport, 1916; dep. dir., mily. lab., E.A.E.F., 1917; lab. comsrr., 1921; asst. sec. for native affrs. Jan., 1922; asst. ch. sec., Jan., 1924; ag. ch. sec., Dec., 1924 to Jan., 1925; ag. dep. ch. sec. in 1927 and 1928; dep. ch. sec., Mar., 1930; ag. ch. sec., May, 1930; ch. sec., June, 1932; ag. gov., Apr.-Nov., 1932.

SCOTT, HENRY HAROLD, M.D., London Univ.; F.R.C.P., London; F.R.S., Edin.; D.P.H.; M.R.C.S., Eng.; D.T.M. & H. (Camb.); Fell. of Royal Soc. of medicine; Fell. of Royal Inst. of preventive medicine; Fell. of Soc. of tropical medicine and hygiene.—Ed. at St. Bart's and St. Thomas's hosps.; Univ. Colls., London and Copenhagen; prosector, 1894; asst. demonstrator in Materia Medica, 1895; asst. house physician, 1897; house physician, 1898, all at St. Thomas's hosp.; res. med. offr., Teignmouth hosp., 1898; serv. in S. African War (Queen's medal with 5 clasps); med. offr. in charge bacteriological and X-Ray depts., mil. hosp., Maritzburg, 1903; M.O. in charge Fort Napier hosp. for women and children, 1904; res. med. offr., Kingbury and Neasden isolation hosp., 1910; bacteriologist to Willesden Dist. Coun., 1910; govt. bacteriologist and fermentation chemist, Jamaica, 1910; is also pathologist to Kingston gen. hosp.; mem. of med. coun., board of examiners, quarantine board, and cent. board of health, Jamaica; during 1915-1917, seconded for war service; bacteriologist at Command Laboratory, Aldershot, 1915; in charge No. XIII, mobile laboratory, 1916; pathologist and med. specialist, Cambridge hosp., Aldershot, 1916; govt. pathologist, dir., serum inst. Hong Kong, 1919; lect. on path. and med. jurisprudence, Hong Kong Univ., 1919; Milner research fellowship, L.S.H. and T.M., 1925; lect., trop. disease, Westminster hosp. med. schl., 1926; examr., D.M.T. and H. Eng., 1927; med. sec., col. med. research comte, 1928.

SCOTT, HENRY SEPTIMUS.—B. 1873; ed. at Eton and Hertford Coll., Oxford; M.A.; inspr. of schools, Transvaal, 1902; examr., 1908; sec. to educn. dept., Transvaal, 1911; dir. of educn., Transvaal, 1924; dir., educn., Kenya, 1928.

SCOTT, SIR JOHN, K.B.E. (1932), C.M.G. (1923).—B. 1878; ed. Bath Coll. and King's Coll., Cambridge (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. ser., Nov., 1901; prin. asst. col. sec., Apr., 1917; dep. ch. sec. to govt., Nigeria, Feb., 1921; ch. sec., Tanganyika Territory, Jan., 1924; admstr. govt. for various periods, 1924-29; col. sec., S. S., 1929; admstr. govt., Oct., 1929 to Feb., 1930 and from Oct., 1930 to June, 1931.

SCOTT, MARGARET.—Ed. Sherbourne Schl. for Girls; V.A.D. nurse, Brit. R. Cross, 1915-19; housekeeper's dipl., Edin. Sch. of Domestic Econ., 1920; matron, Achimota, 1925.

SCOTT, R. R., M.C., M.B., B.S. (Durham), M.R.C.S. (Eng.), L.R.C.P. (Lond.), D.P.H. (Lond.)—R.A.M.C. (S.R.), Aug., 1914; ment. in depts., 1919; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Mar., 1919; senr. med. offr. of health, Apr., 1924; dep. dir., sanry. serv., 1932.

SCOTT, WALTER RICHARDSON.—B. 1899; ed. Durham, 1922; pol. probationer, Hong Kong, 1922; passed final exam. in Chinese, 1924; asst. supt. pol., 1924; J.P., 1925; attd. Indian pol. and passed in Urdu 1926; passed Punjabi, 1928; pvt. sec. to O.A.G., in addn., 1928; ditto to gov. in addn., Jan. to Mar., 1929; hon. A.D.C. to gov., 1929; ag. dir., crim. intell., 1932-33; supt. pol., 1933.

SCRIVENER, RUPERT FREDERICK.—B. 1890; assoc., R. Sch. of Mines, dipl., Imp. Coll. Science, assoc., I.M.M., assoc., Inst. of Mining and Metallurgy; survey work, England and Alaska, 1911-14; comsmd. serv., 1914-20; capt., 1918; served at Gallipoli, Egypt, Mesopotamia, India and Palestine; commanded, 29th Rly. Coy., Sapper and Miners, I.A.; asst. chg. engnr., Palestine rly., 1920; engrnr., ways and wks., Palestine rly., 1924.

SCRIVENER, T. V.—B. 1908; ed. King Schl., Canterbury and Oriel Coll., Oxford; B.A., 1930; apptd. temp. asst. prin., C.O., Oct., 1931; prior to serv. as an admstr. offr., N. Rhodesia.

SCULLIN, Rt. Hon. JAMES HENRY, P.C.—El. to Commonwealth H. of R. for Corangamite, Victoria, 1910; defeated, gen. el., 1913; M.H.R. for Yarra, Victoria, since 1922; prime min. of the Commonwealth of Australia, 1929-31.

SEAGOK, ERNEST GOLDFINCH, M.B.E.—B. 1886; clk. to res. comsrr., New Hebrides, 1902; inspr. of native labourers, Br. residency, New Hebrides, 1909; ag. asst. to res. comsrr., 1911-12 and 1915-16; joint ag. native advocate, Oct., 1915, to Dec., 1922; ag. asst. to res., Nov., 1919 to Feb., 1920 and Sept. to Dec., 1921; commt. constab., Aug., 1922; dep. comsrr., W. Pacific (New Hebrides), Nov., 1922; in ch. of acts., May to Aug., 1923; ag. asst. to res. comsrr., on various occasions, 1923-31; dist. agt. and lab. inspr., Apr., 1923; agt., Efate dist. and commt. pol. (Br. divn.), Apr., 1925.

SEDGWICK, RICHARD ROMNEY.—B. 1894; ed. Westminster and Trinity Coll., Cambridge; schol., Trinity Coll., 1912; lat. cl. hist. trips, pt. I, 1914 and pt. II, 1915; Gladstone prem., 1914; elected fellow of Trinity Coll., 1919; M.A., 1919; apptd. under reconstruction scheme asst. prin., Min. of Labour, 1919; asst. prin., C.O., 1922; pvt. sec. to under. sec. of State, D.O., 23rd Sept., 1929; prin., D.O., 1st Oct., 1930.

SEDWICK, NATHANIEL ASHER.—B. 1890; ed. Univ. Coll., Schl., London, and St. Peter's Coll., Camb.; B.A., London and Camb.; cadet, S.S., Dec., 1913; dep. to supt., govt. monopolies dep., Jan., 1914; in charge of govt. opium factory, Mar. to Aug., 1914; passed cadet (Malay), Mar., 1917; attd., col. sec.'s office, Apr., 1917; coll. ed. war tax, Singapore, July, 1918; supervm. offr., cls. IV., Nov., 1920; offr., cls. III., Nov., 1929; lat. mag. and pres., town bd., Johore Bahru, Oct., 1930; offr., cls. II., Nov., 1930; asst. treas., Penang, Nov., 1932.

SEED, CHARLES WILLIAM STANLEY.—B. 1889; ed. St. John's (R.C.) Coll., Wonthaggi, Nurney Artists' Rifles, 1916; 2nd lieut., 12th Leicestershire Regt., 1917; served in France, 1918-19; (D.S.O. and Victory Meds.); col. audit dept., July, 1921; asst. audr., Nigeria, Sept., 1921; ag. senr. audr., July-Sept., 1926; asst. audr., Nyasaland, Dec., 1926; ag. senr. audr., audr., June, 1927 to July, 1928 and Oct., 1928 to Sept., 1929; audr., Seychelles and Somaliland, July, 1930.

SEEL, GEORGE FREDERICK.—B. 1895; ed. Macclesfield Grammar Schl. and Corpus Christi...
Coll., Oxford (schol.); on mily. serv. Cheshire Regt. in Gallipoli, Egypt and Palestine; apptd. to air mily., 28th July, 1919; seconded for serv. in C.O., as ast. privy. sec., 9th Jan., 1922; pvt. sec. to parly. under secy. of state for the Cols. (Mr. Wm. Lunn, M.P.), 10th June, 1929; prin., 17th Sept., 1929.

SEELY, MAJOR-GEN. RT. HON. JOHN EDWARD BERNARD, P.C. (1909), C.B. (1916), C.M.G. (1918), D.S.O. (1900).—Ed. at Harrow and Trinity Coll., Cambridge; called to the bar, Inner Temple, 1897; lieut.-col. commdg. Hampshire Carabiniers; served with Imperial Yeomanry in S. Africa, 1900-1901 (despa., Queen's medal, five clasps, D.S.O.); M.P. for Isle of Wight, 1900-06; M.P. for Abercromby div., Liverpool, 1906-1910; M.P. for Ilkeston div., Derbyshire, 1910; recd. gold medal (French govt.) for saving life at sea, 1891; parly. under-secr. of state for the colonies, 1908; chmn. of comtees to inquire into organisation of crown agents office, 1908; under-secr. of state for war, 1911; sec. of state for war, 1912-14; joint parly. sec. to ministry of munitions, 1918; under-secr. of state for air, Jan., 1919.

SEHEULT, JOSEPH EMMANUEL.—B. 1881; entd. civ. serv., Trinidad, Mar., 1902; oh. clk., dept. of agric., Jan., 1916; ast. censor, 1914; censor, Apr., 1918; man.-sec., agric. bank, Jan., 1928.

SEHEULT, LEO GABRIEL, M.I.C.E., A.C.G.I.—B. 1886; ast. dist. offr., pub. works, Trinidad, Mar., 1911; 2nd grade dist. offr., Sept., 1916; 1st grade dist. offr., June, 1917; gen. ast. to ast. D.P.W., Jan., 1925.

SEIGNORET, G. B.—Clk. to postmr., Dominica, 1889; govt. offr., treasy., 1893; oh. clk., registr.'s off., 1895; ag. postmr., 1896-7; olk. govt. offr., Roseau, 1897; govt. offr., treasy., 1901, postmr., 1925.

SELBORNE, 2nd EARL OF (creat. 1882), VISCOUNT WOLMER, BARON SELBORNE (U.K.), K.G. (1909), P.C. (1900), G.C.M.G. (1905). THE RT. HON. WM. WALDEGRAVE PALMER.—B. 1859; ed. at Winchester and at Univ. Coll., Oxford; B.A. (1st cls. hist.), 1882; ast. priv. sec. to Mr. Childers, Chanc. of Excheq., 1882-85; was mem. of parlmt. for E. Hants, 1885-92, and for W. Edinburgh City, 1892-96; succeeded his father, 1896; Under S. of S. for Cols., June, 1895; chmn. Pacific cable comtee., 1896; mem. of Pacific cable comtee., 1899; first lord of the admiralty, Nov. 12th, 1900; high comnrsr. for S. Africa, and gov. and comdr-in-chief of Transvaal and O.R.C., 1905 to 1910; ceased to be gov. of O.R.C. on grant of resp. govt., June, 1907; pres. of bd. of agric. and fisheries, 1915-16.

SELBY, JOHN ALEXANDER ROBERTSON, M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.)—B. 1900; venereal diseases offr., med. dep., Hong Kong, 1930.

SELDON, ARTHUR ARNOLD.—B. 1889; ed. Charterhouse and Oriel Coll., Oxford, B.A. (hons.); ast. dist. comsnr., E.A.F., Dec., 1913; capt., K.A.R., 1917-18; sec., famine comtee., Nairobi, 1919; personal ast. to ch. native comsnr., 1920; 1st grade admstve. offr., 1925; H.M.'s ag. consul, S. Abyssinia, 1928.

SELLS, MARTIN PERROW, O.B.E., A.M.I.M.E. M.I.Loco. E.—B. 1887; ed. Trent Coll. and Univ. Coll., London; junr. ast. loco. supt., Lancs and Yorks. Rly.; temp. major R.E., 1917; supt., light rlya., France, 1917-1919 (twice ment. in desps.); dist. loco. supt., Tanganyika Terry. rlya., 1919; ag. ch. mech. engnr., Tanganyika Terry. rlya., 1920; ch. mech. engnr., Gold Coast rlya., 1922; ch. mech. engnr., Nigerian Rly., 1926.

SELWYN-CLARKE, PERCY SELWYN, M.C., M.D., B.S. (Lond.), M.R.C.P. (Lond.), M.R.C.S. (Eng.), D.P.H. (Eng.) with distinc., D.T.M. and H. (Lond.), barrister-at-law.—B. 1893; ed. St. Bartholomew's Hosp. and Lond. Univ.; med. offr., W.A.M.S., Oct., 1919; med. offr., health, W.A.M.S., Gold Coast, Nov., 1919; senr. san. offr., W.A.M.S., Oct., 1924; awarded Langley Memorial Prize, 1924; dep. dir., san. serv., May to Aug., 1927; del. for Gold Coast to Yellow Fever confee., Dakar, Senegal, 1928; visited U.S.A. and Canada at invitation of Rockefeller Foundation, 1928; ast. dir., san. serv., June, 1929; called to bar, Gray's Inn, 1929; awarded Médaille d'Argent des Épidémies for work in connection with outbreak of yellow fever in W. SMITH, P. P. O., Assoc. M.Inst.C.E., A.M.I. Mech.E.—B. 1881; ed. London Univ.; mily. serv., France, with R.E.'s; awarded Croix de Guerre, ment. in despr.; Reg. Army, R. of O., 1916-19; astt. engrnr., 1st grade, Lagos harbr. wks., 1920; senr. astt. engrnr., harbr. dept., Lagos, Apr., 1927.

SMITH, REGINALD HOPKINSON.—B. 1898; ed. Chatham House, Ramsgate; served in the Royal Naval Divn., Oct. to Dec., 1914; H.A.C., Oct., 1915 to Oct., 1917; Indian Army R. of O., Nov., 1917 to Aug., 1919; Aden Field Force, July, 1918 to July, 1919; dist. pol. offr., Somaliland, July, 1919.

SMITH, ROBERT EDMUND, B.A. (Cantab.).—B. 1881; astt. mast., Outram Rd. Schl., Singapore, Aug., 1906; ditto, Raffles Inst., Nov., 1907, July, 1912, and Oct., 1913; headmast., Victoria Bridge Schl., Singapore, Mar., 1922.

SMITH, SIDNEY W.—B. 1892; apptd., after compet. exam., astt. clk., C.O., Oct., 1919; cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920; higher grade cler. offr., 29th Oct., 1930.

SMITH, STEPHEN HENRY, C.B.E. (1929), F.R. Aus. H.S.—B. 1865; ed. Grafton Superior Pub. Sch.; inspr., continuation schls., N. S. Wales, June, 1912 to Feb., 1920; astt. under sec., educn. dept., N.S.W., June, 1920; dir., educn., N.S.W., 1923.

SMITH, STEPHEN JOHN.—B. 1887; N.Z. post and tel. dept., 1903; internal affrs. dept., 1913; sec., Samoan admstrn., 1915; ch. clk., external affrs. dept., 1920-30; ch. clk., Cook Is. dept., 1920-28; sec., 1928.

SMITH, WALTER JOHN.—B. 1884; astt. supt. wks., P.W.D., S. SMITH, WILLIAM FORGAN, M.L.A. (Queensland).—B. and ed. in Scotland; M.L.A., Queensland since 1915; successively min. without portfolio, sec. for pub. wks. and sec. for agr. and stock; premier and treas., June, 1932.

SMITH, WILLIAM HARDEN, B.A., M.B., B.Ch., B.A.O. (T.C.D.), L.M. (Rot.), D.P.H. (R.C.P. and S.I.), D.T.M. (Calcutta).—ed. Trinity Coll., Dublin; surg. sub-lieut., R.N.V.R., 1918; med. offr., Zanzibar, Nov., 1925; ag. D.D.S.S., on various occasions, 1930-33.

SMITH, WILLIAM HUMPHREY.—B. 1879; ed. SMUTS, GEN. THE RIGHT HON. J. C., P.C. (1917), C.H., K.C.—B. 1870; ed. at Victa Coll., Stellenbosch; B.A., Cape Univ., 1890; Ebden scholar at Christ's Coll., Camb.; doc. first in law tripes, 1894; barrister, Caps Co.; state-attorney, S. African war, and was in comd. of Boer forces in Cape Col. during the latter part of the campaign; mem. of boel comte. of Het Volk; col. sec., Transvaal, 1907; mem. of Imp. Africa, 1916; mem. of British war cabinet; represented S. Africa at peace confce. at Paris, 1919; prime min. and min. of native affrs., Union of S. Africa, 1919-24; M.P. for Standerton, 1924; leader, opposition, 1924-33; pres., Br. Assn. for Advancement of Science, 1931; min. of just. and dep. prime-min. coalition govt., 1933; leader, S. African deleg., World Economic Confce., 1933.

SMYLY, Sir PHILIP CRAMPTON, KT, Bar. (1905).—B. 1866; ed. at Trin. Coll., Dub., B.A., LL.B.; called to the bar, King's Inns, Dub., 1887; LL.D., 1891; called to the bar, Gray's Inn, 1897; Queen's advoc., S. Leone, 1898; atty.-gen., 1898; ch. just., S. Leone, 1901; ch. just., Gold Coast, 1911; ret., 1929.

SNELGAR, HERBERT JOHN.—B. 1890; ed. Christ's Hosp. and Kings Coll., London; clk. ed. of educn., 1906; clk., C.A., 1910; clk., land dept., E.A.P., 1912; ag. office supt., 1917 and 1919; land astt., 1919; sec., land tenure comm., 1920; warden of mines, 1920; regar. of titles, etc., 1922; astt. land offr., 1922.

SNELL, EDWARD WALTER.—B. 1879; astt. post office, Kingwilliamstown, Mar., 1900; astt. G.P.O., Cape Town, Nov., 1900; clk., area branch, July, 1903; 1st cls. clk., Ap., 1912; income tax office, Pretoria, Sept., 1914; sec. clk., income tax office, Cape Town, July, 1915; senior clk., rev. office, Johannesburg, May, 1918; prin. clk., ditto, Jan., 1921; ch. clk., income tax, head office, inland rev. dept., Pretoria, Aug., 1921; astt. commr., inland rev., Sept., 1929.

SNYMAN, NICOLAAS.—Prof. astt. to surv. gen., O.F.S., 1920; survr.-gen., O.F.S., inc., 1931.

SOLLIS, CLIFFORD GEORGE, B.A.—B. 1876; ed. Bristol Grammar Schl. and St. John's Coll., Oxford; astt. mast., Bukit Zahrah Sch., Johor Bahru, Dec., 1920; ag. inspr., schls. Patani, Oct., 1925; do., Mar., 1928; supt., educn., Kedah, Dec., 1930; inspr., schls., Selangor, Aug., 1931.
SOLOMON, NEVILLE STAFFORD VICTOR.—B. 1874; clk., G.P.O., Bahamas, 1891; tel. dept., 1892; treas. and cust., 1895; supervisor, cust., 2nd gde., Gold Coast, 1902; ag. ch. reg. inst., sup. ot., 1906; finan. ast., treas. and cust. dept., Nigeria, 1907; supervisor, 1st gde., cust. dept., 1910; collr., 1917; adm. reporting offr., various ports, Nigeria, during great war, 1914-18; ret. on pension, 1922; ast. postm. (temp.), Bahamas, Jan., 1924; resigned, Nov., 1925; recr. gen. and treas., mem. exec. coun., Bahamas, 1928; mem., leg. coun., Feb., 1931; chmn., licensing authority, Mar., 1931; has held various ag. appts.

SOLOMON, SARL.—B. 1875; ed. Bedford Grammar Schl. and Lincoln Coll., Oxford; M.A.; called to bar, Lincoln's Inn, 1900; K.C.; mem. of S. Africa, 1919; judge, sup. ct., Transvaal prov. divn., 1927.

SOMASUNTHARAM, KANDIAH.—B. 1897; cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Dec., 1921; attd. Kalutara kach., Dec., 1921; ditto, Kurunegala kach., Jan., 1922; ditto, Colombo Kach., Dec., 1922; office ast. to rubber contr., Mar., 1923; office ast., Galle kach., Aug., 1926; 6th ast. col. sec., Nov., 1926; 4th ast. col. sec., May, 1928; addnl. ast. gov't. agt., Colombo, Jan., 1929; addnl. ast. contr. rev., Nov., 1929; ast. gov't. agt., Kurunegala, July, 1931; dist. judge, Kegalla, July, 1932.

SOMERS (6TH BARON, OR. 1784), ARTHUR HERBERT SOMERS COOKE, K.C.M.G. (1926), D.S.O. (1919), M.C. (1917).—B. 1887; ed. Charterhouse and New Coll., Oxford; serv. in Great War, 1914-19; capt., 1st Life Guards, 1914; lieut.-col., Tank Corps, 1918-19; ret., 1922; a lord in waiting in ordinary to the King, 1924; gov'r. of Victoria, 1926-31.

SOMERS, CECIL GEORGE.—B. 1896; served Dardanelles and E. Mediterranean with H.M. Transports, 1914-18; gov't. pilot, Kenya, 1924; ast. port offr., Zanzibar, 1929; ag. port offr., Aug., 1929 to Mar., 1930 and Apr. to Dec., 1932.

SOPER, JOHN ROBERT PHILPOTT, B.A. (hons.), Cantab.—B. 1904; ed. Tonbridge Schol. and Pembroke Coll., Cambridge (schol.); headmaster, agr. prim. schl., Zanzibar, Sept., 1926; seconded for duty as agr. offr., 1926; agr. offr., 1928.

SOUTH, FRANCIS WILTON, M.A. (Cantab.).—B. 1886; ed. Marlborough Coll., and Emmanuel Coll., Cambridge; mycologist and lect. in agr. sci., Imp. dept. of agr. for W. Indies, Mar., 1909; ch. agr. inspnr., agr. dept., F.M.S., May, 1913; ch. agr. field offr., Nov., 1924; ag. sec. for agr., S.S. and F.M.S., for various periods 1927-31; rep. of Malaya at mycological conf. in Lond., Sept., 1929; ag. dir., agr., S.S. and F.M.S. for various periods, 1929 and 1931-32.

SOUTHBOROUGH, 1ST BARON (creat. 1917), RT. HON. SIR FRANCIS JOHN STEPHENS HOPWOOD, P.C. (1912), G.C.B. (1916), G.C.M.G. (1908), K.C.B. (1901), K.C.M.G. (1906), C.B. (1895), C.M.G. (1893).—B. 1860; ed. at Louth by Canon W. W. Hopwood; admitted a solr., 1882; ast. law clk., B. of T., 1885-1888; ast. solr., 1888-1892; priv. sec. to pres. of B. of T., 1892; sec., rly. dept., 1892-1901; perm. sec., 1901; perm. under-secr. of S. for the colonies, 1907-1910; employed on different occasions upon offl. missions to U.S.A., Canada, and Newfoundland; Brit. deleg. to internat. rly. congress in London, 1895; and in Paris, 1900; hon. sec. to chmn. of select comte. of H. of C. on Jameson raid, 1897; mem. of London traffic coman., 1903; visited S. Africa as mem. of Transvaal and O.R.C. constitutions coman., 1906; mem. of comans. on canals and waterways, 1906; and on ocean freights and shipping "rings," 1906; accompanied H.R.H. the Prince of Wales on his visit to Quebec, 1908; mem. of Royal coman. on electoral reform, 1909; reg. of the Order of St. Michael and St. George, 1907-1909; sec. of the Order, 1909-1911; accompanied H.R.H. the Duke of Connaught on his visit to S. Africa in connection with the opening of the first parlmt. of the Union of S. Africa, 1910; vice-chmn. of the Development coman., 1910; specially apptd. to act as under sec. of state for the colonies during the period of the Imperial Conf., 1911; additional civil lord of the Admiralty, Jan., 1912; sec. to the Irish Convention, 1917.

SOUTHHORN, SIR WILFRID THOMAS, K.B.E. (1933), C.M.G. (1927).—B. 1879; ed. Warwick schl. and Corpus Christi Coll., Oxford (B.A.); cadet, Ceylon civ. serv., Nov., 1903; off. ast. to gov't. agt., N. Prov., Oct., 1904; N.C. Prov., May, 1905; dist. judge, Tangalla, Apr., 1907; landing survr. customs, Colombo, July, 1909; ast. gov't. agt., Matale, Nov., 1911; priv. sec. to gov', Aug., 1914; dep. collr. of customs and landing survr., Colombo, Sept., 1915; 2nd ast. col. sec., Dec., 1919; prin. ast. col. sec., July, 1920; prin. collr., cust. and chmn., Colombo port coman., Dec., 1923; mem., leg. coun., 1923 and exec. coun., 1923; col. sec., Hong Kong, May, 1926; O.A.G., in 1927, 1928, 1929, 1930 and 1932.

SPAFFORD, H. H., B.A.—B. 1899; instr., schls., Gold Coast, Jan., 1928.

SPEARMAN, BARUGH, O.B.E. (1934), M.A., M.B., B.C. (Camb.), D.T.M. and H., certif., London Schol. of Trop. Medicine (with distinc.), F.R. Sany. SPEED, SIR EDWIN ARNET, KT. B.A.C. (1911).—M.A., LL.B.; B. 1869; ed. at Rugby, and Trin. Coll., Camb.; major scholar and senior exhibtr., Rugby schl.; scholar and prizeman of Trin. Nigeria, May, 1906; edited revised edtn. of laws of S. Nigeria, 1907; ch. just., N. Nigeria, 1908; retired.

SPEIRS, R. C., M.B., Ch.B. (Edin.), D.T.M. (Liv.)—B. 1901; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Apr., 1925.
SPICER, Roy Godfrey Bullen, M.C. (1918).—B. 1889; ed. Colet Court and St. Paul's; probationary asst. supt. pol., Ceylon, Nov., 1909; asst. supt., 1911; 1915; on war serv., 1915-19; wounded, Oct., 1918; returned to Ceylon pol., 1919; supt., grade I, 1923; comanr. pol., Kenya, June, 1925; comdt., pol., Palestine, 1930.

SPILLER, John Wyatt, M.Inst.C.E.—B. 1878; ed. Wellington Schol. SPRING, Frederick George, N.D.A., U.D.A., F.L.S.—B. 1887; supt., govt. plantations, F.M.S., Sept., 1910; agriculturist, agrl. dept., May, 1912; agriculturist (rubber), Jan., 1925; sec. to co-op. societies dept., May, 1927.

STACPOOLE, George Wentworth.—Asst. commr., lands survey dept., Gold Coast, 1925; transf. to lands dept., 1927; ag. dep. commr., July, 1928-Apr., 1929; ag. commr., lands, Apr.-Oct., 1932.

STAFFORD, Frank Edmund.—B. 1895; ed. R. STANLEY, Sir Herbert James, G.C.M.G. (1930), K.C.M.G. (1924), C.M.G. (1913).—B. 1872; ed. at Eton and Balliol Coll., Oxford (M.A.); priv. sec. to H.M. min. resident at Dresden and Coburg, and British vice-consul at Dresden, 1897-1902; asst. priv. sec. to first Lord of the Admiralty, 1906-1908; priv. sec. to Lord Pres. of the Coun., 1908-1910; priv. sec. to Viscount Gladstone, gen. gen. of Union of S. Africa, 1910; sec. to gov. gen., 1913; resident commr., Southern and Northern Rhodesia, 1st Apr., 1915; Imperial sec. and acctnt. to high commr. for S. Africa, 1918; first gov. and commdr.-in-chief, N. Rhodesia, 1st Apr., 1924; gov. of Ceylon, July, 1927; high commr. for the U.K. in the Union of S. Africa, 1931.

STANLEY, W. B., C.M.G. (1923), M.B.E. (1918), Barrister-at-Law, Gray's Inn, 1921.—Served with 1st Border regt. occupation of Crete, 1898; S. Africa, 1899-1900 (med. and 4 clasps); 2nd lieut., W. India regt., 1900; lieut., 1901; ag. adjt., 3rd W. India regt., Gambia expd., 1901, (med. and clasps); ag. trav. commr., Gambia May and June, 1901; trav. commr., Gambia, Aug., 1901; A.D.C. and priv. sec. to ag. gov., Gambia, Aug. to Oct., 1901; capt., 1902; passed course of survey, schl. of mil. eng., Chatham, 1905; resig. commr., 1906; capt., 1st Yorks regt., 1906; qualified in native language; dist. commr., S. STANTON, Ambrose Thomas, C.M.G. (1929), M.D., F.R.C.P., D.P.H., D.T.M. and H.—B. 1875; sen. house surg. (to Sir Patrick Maloney), hosp. for trop. diseases, 1905; asst. Inst. for Med. STAPLES, James Webster.—B. 1902; appd. after compet. exam., asst. clk., G.P.O., Oct., 1919; cler. offr., 1st Jan., 1920; transf. to C.O., Mar., 1923.

STAPLEY, Frank R.—B. 1893; mily. serr., Sept., 1914 to Dec., 1919; temp. clk., C.O., Apr., 1920; appd. cler. offr., 4th July, 1922; higher grade cler. offr., 17th Feb., 1930.

STATHAM, Hon. Sir Charles Ernest Ky. Bach. (1926).—Mem., N.Z. parl. since 1915; speaker since 1923.

STEAD, Kingsley Williams, C.B.E. (1933), O.B.E. (1928).—B. 1883; ed. at King Edward's Birmingham; apptd., after open compet. exam., asst. in impl. cust., Cardiff, Mar., 1903; Harwich, Oct., 1906; asst. collr. of cust., Larnaca, Cyprus, dep. harbr. and tide supervisor, Apr., 1908; collr. of cust. and excise, Apr., 1910; passed prelim. exam. in modern Greek, June, 1910; reg. of trade marks, June, 1911; passed lower standard exam.in modern Greek, June, 1912; asst. cable censor, Aug., 1914-Apr., 1919; cable censor, May-July, 1919; pub. cust. of enemy property, Jan.-July, 1920; refugee commr., Larnaca, May-1919 to Apr., 1920; reg. of patents, Aug.-Sept., 1920; ch. collr. of cust. and excise, Oct., 1921; mpr. of fisheries, 1921; Médaille de la Reconnaissance Française, 3rd cls., 1922; ag. commr., Larnaca for various periods in 1922, 1923 and 1924; reg. of companies, July, 1922; ch. supt. STEED, L. F.—B. 1897; on mily. serv., Sept., 1914 to Mar., 1919; temp. elk., O.S.O., Feb.
STEEL, Cecil Richard, M.R.C.S. (Eng.) L.R.C.P. (Lond.), Cert. London S.H.T.M. (distinct) D.T.M. & H. (Eng.)—Mily. serv., 1917-19; med. offr., Tanganyika Territory, Jan., 1925.

STEPHENS, John Edward Robert.—B. 1869; ed. St. Olave's Schl., York and Royal Univ. of Ireland; called to the bar, Middle Temp., 1894; mag., H.B.M. ct., Zanzibar, Jan., 1912, and mag. of the ct. of H.H. the Sultan of Zanzibar, Feb., 1912; ag. asst. judge, Aug., 1915 to Apr., 1916 and from Feb. to Aug., 1918; 3rd puisane judge, Kenya, Feb., 1925; editor-in-ch. of "The Manual of Naval Law and Court-martial procedure" (4th edn.); asst. editor of 11th edn. of "Addison on Contracts"; author of works on "Demurrage," "Freight," "Charter parties," etc.; contributor to the Encyclopedia of the Laws of England, Journal of Comparative Legislation, etc.

STEWART, ROBERT STROTHER, M.A., B.C.L., B.Lit., Durham Univ., Gladstone prizeman.—Admitted solr., sup. ct., 1905; 2nd lieut. the Tynemouth R.G.A. (T.F.), 1913; A.D.C. to gen. offr., commdg. STEWART, HON. WILLIAM DOWNE, LL.B.—B. 1878; ed. Otago High Schl. and Otago Univ.; ent. N.Z. parl., 1914; served in France with N.Z. Rifle Brig.; min. of intern. affrs., 1921-23; min. of cust., 1921-28; min. of industries and commerce, 1923-26; atty.-gen., Jan.-May, 1926; min. of finance and min. of stamp duties, 1926-28; also atty.-gen., min. of just., and min. of defence, Nov.-Dec., 1928; joined coalition miny. as min. of finance, cust., and stamp duties, and atty.-gen., 1931; ret. from miny., 1933; negotiated N.Z.-Canada trade treaty, 1932; mem., N.Z. delegation at Ottawa confce., 1932.

STEYEN, DANIEL, B.A. (Cape Town), LL.B. (Univ. of S. Africa).—B. 1893; senr. mast., Boshoff Schl. and Gymnasium, Paarl, 1917; judge's regar., O.F.S., 1920; pvt. sec. to prime min., 1924; Union consul-gen., Lourenco Marques, Sept., 1929.

STIRLING, JOHN WIGHTMAN.—B. 1885; med. offr., Basuto Land, 1912.
